title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Ask favours politely, offer and accept or refuse, invite people and respond to invitations, using respectful forms.
intro:
Politeness in Kannada lives mostly in the **verb forms** rather than in words like 'please'. Using the respectful plural (ನೀವು, ಅವರು, ಬನ್ನಿ, ಕೂತ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ) for anyone older or unfamiliar, and phrasing requests as questions ('will you give?'), matters far more than ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು.

This unit also introduces the **optative** -ಲಿ ('let it be, may it be') and the 'shall I?' form -ಲಾ, which are essential for offers and blessings.

vocab.note: ಸಹಾಯ ಮಾಡು 'to help'. Spoken also ಹೆಲ್ಪ್.
ತುಂಬಾ ಉಪಕಾರ ಆಯ್ತು 'you've been a great help'.
Used in Mysuru region to address men respectfully.
-ಇ ಕೊಡು adds 'for someone': ಹೇಳಿಕೊಡು 'teach', ತೋರಿಸಿಕೊಡು 'show (someone how)'.
Irregular, like ಬರು: imperative ತಾ / ತನ್ನಿ; past ತಂದೆ tande.

phrases.en: Could you help me a little?
Could you do me a favour?
Come for a meal on Sunday.
Sorry, I can't come that day.
All the best! (lit. may good happen)
Would you teach me a little Kannada?

grammar.title: Polite requests and honorifics
grammar.body:
Ways to make a request, from blunt to very polite:
1. Informal imperative: ಕೊಡು 'give' (only to close friends/children)
2. Polite imperative: ಕೊಡಿ 'please give'
3. Softened: ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕೊಡಿ / ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು ಕೊಡಿ
4. As a question in the future ('will you?'): **ಕೊಡ್ತೀರಾ?** 'would you give?' – the most natural polite request
5. Very formal: ದಯಮಾಡಿ ಕೊಡಬೇಕು / ಕೊಡಬೇಕಾಗಿ ವಿನಂತಿ (written)

**Doing something for someone** = past participle + **ಕೊಡು**: ಮಾಡಿ ಕೊಡಿ 'do it for me', ಬರೆದು ಕೊಡಿ 'write it down for me', ಹೇಳಿಕೊಡಿ 'teach me'.

**Honorifics**: always use the plural ನೀವು / ಅವರು and plural verb endings for elders, teachers, in-laws, officials and strangers: ಅಪ್ಪ ಬಂದರು 'Father came' rather than ಅಪ್ಪ ಬಂದ. Respectful titles follow the name: ರಾವ್ ಅವರು, ಲಕ್ಷ್ಮಿ ಅವರು (like 'Mr/Ms'), or kinship terms (ಅಣ್ಣ, ಅಕ್ಕ, ಅಂಕಲ್). For very elevated people, verbs like ಊಟ ಮಾಡಿ (rather than ತಿನ್ನಿ) and ಕುಳಿತುಕೊಳ್ಳಿ (rather than ಕೂತ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ) sound more refined.

examples.en: Could you write down this address for me?
Could you speak a bit more slowly?

grammar.title: Offers, 'let', and blessings: -ಲಾ, -ಓಣ, -ಲಿ
grammar.body:
**'Shall I?'** (offers) = infinitive + **-ಲಾ** (written standard -ಲೇ: ಮಾಡಲೇ?; in fast speech the a drops: ಮಾಡ್ಲಾ?): ತರು → ತರಲಾ? 'shall I bring?', ಮಾಡು → ಮಾಡಲಾ? / ಮಾಡ್ಲಾ? 'shall I do it?', ಬರಲಾ? 'shall I come? / may I go now?' (leave-taking).

**'Let's'** = -ಓಣ (unit 11); **'Shall we?'** = -ಓಣವಾ? / -ಓಣ್ವಾ?

**Optative 'let him / may it'** = infinitive + **-ಲಿ**:
• ಅವನು ಬರಲಿ 'let him come'
• ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದಾಗಲಿ 'may good happen to you' = all the best
• ದೇವರು ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದು ಮಾಡಲಿ 'may God bless you'
• ಇರಲಿ 'let it be, never mind'
• ಕ್ಷಮೆ ಇರಲಿ 'please forgive me (lit. let there be forgiveness)'

**Refusing politely**: Kannadigas rarely say a flat ಇಲ್ಲ. Use ಬೇಡ, ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ 'no need, it's fine', ಈಗ ಬೇಡ 'not now', ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಸಲ 'another time', or ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಕಷ್ಟ 'that's a bit difficult'. Hosts will insist two or three times; refusing once is expected modesty.

examples.en: Okay, shall I take my leave?
Let the children play, leave them.
Never mind, I'll come another time.

dialogue.title: A housewarming invitation
dialogue.setting: Mrs. Bhat visits her new neighbour Claire to invite her to a ಗೃಹಪ್ರವೇಶ (housewarming).

lines.speaker: Bhat
lines.native: ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ! ನಾನು ಪಕ್ಕದ ಮನೆಯವಳು, ಸುಮಾ ಭಟ್.
lines.roman: namaskāra! nānu pakkada maneyavaḷu, sumā bhaṭ.
lines.en: Hello! I'm from next door, Suma Bhat.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.en: Hello! Come, come in. Please sit.

lines.speaker: Bhat
lines.native: ಇಲ್ಲ, ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ, ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಅರ್ಜೆಂಟ್. ಭಾನುವಾರ ನಮ್ಮ ಮನೆ ಗೃಹಪ್ರವೇಶ. ನೀವು ಖಂಡಿತ ಬರಬೇಕು.
lines.roman: illa, paravāgilla, svalpa arjeṇṭ. bhānuvāra namma mane gruhapravēsha. nīvu khaṇḍita barabēku.
lines.en: No, it's okay, I'm in a bit of a hurry. Sunday is our housewarming. You must come.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.native: ಓಹ್, ಅಭಿನಂದನೆಗಳು! ಸಂತೋಷದಿಂದ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ. ಎಷ್ಟು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ?
lines.roman: ōh, abhinandanegaḷu! santōṣadinda bartīni. eṣṭu gaṇṭege?
lines.en: Oh, congratulations! I'll gladly come. What time?

lines.speaker: Bhat
lines.native: ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ ಪೂಜೆ ಇದೆ, ಹನ್ನೆರಡು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಊಟ. ನಿಮ್ಮ ಯಜಮಾನರನ್ನೂ ಕರ್ಕೊಂಡು ಬನ್ನಿ.
lines.roman: beḷigge pūje ide, hanneraḍu gaṇṭege ūṭa. nimma yajamānarannū karkoṇḍu banni.
lines.en: There's a puja in the morning, lunch at twelve. Do bring your husband too.

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.en: Sure. If you need any help, just say.

lines.speaker: Bhat
lines.native: ತುಂಬಾ ಉಪಕಾರ. ಕಾಫಿ ಕುಡಿಯೋಕೆ ಸಮಯ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಕ್ಷಮೆ ಇರಲಿ. ಬರ್ಲಾ?
lines.roman: tumbā upakāra. kāphi kuḍiyōke samaya illa, kṣame irali. barlā?
lines.en: That's very kind. I don't have time for coffee, forgive me. Shall I head off?

lines.speaker: Claire
lines.en: Okay, goodbye. See you on Sunday!

culture: When invited to a home, it's polite to bring fruit or sweets (not flowers by default), to remove shoes at the door, and to accept at least a glass of water or coffee: refusing everything can seem cold. Married women visiting a home are often given ಅರಿಶಿನ-ಕುಂಕುಮ (turmeric and vermilion) and a blouse piece or betel leaves when they leave. ಬರ್ಲಾ? (lit. 'shall I come?', short for ಹೋಗಿ ಬರ್ಲಾ? 'shall I go and come back?') is a common polite way to ask leave, alongside ಹೋಗಿ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ / ಬರ್ತೀನಿ.

tip.title: Asking nicely: "will you…?"
tip.body:
- The most natural polite request is a **will-you question**: ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ನೀರು **ಕೊಡ್ತೀರಾ?** 'could you give me some water?'
- Softer with **ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ** or **ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು**; very formal **ದಯಮಾಡಿ**.
- For someone: -ಇ form + **ಕೊಡು**: ಬರೆದು ಕೊಡ್ತೀರಾ? 'would you write it for me?'
- Elders and strangers always get the plural: ತಂದೆ ಇದ್ದಾ**ರಾ**?

sentences.en: Could you give me some water?
Could you show me the way to the station?
Could you wait five minutes?
Could you come with me for a moment?
Could you write this down for me in Kannada?
Kindly come in.
Is your father at home?
Sorry to trouble you.
You've been a great help.

tip.title: Offers: -ಲಾ? and saying no nicely
tip.body:
- **Shall I?** = verb + **-ಲಾ?**: ತರ**ಲಾ**? 'shall I bring it?', ಮಾಡಲಾ? 'shall I make it?'
- Bring is irregular: **ತನ್ನಿ** 'please bring', past ತಂದೆ.
- To say no, avoid a flat ಇಲ್ಲ: **ಬೇಡ, ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ** 'no need, it's fine'. Hosts ask two or three times.

sentences.en: Shall I make some tea?
Shall I bring you something to eat?
No thanks, I've already eaten.
Shall I bring your bag?
Please bring that book tomorrow.
Shall I shut the door?
Shall I call an auto?
It's getting late, we'll be off now.
He fixed my phone for me.

sentences.native: ಶನಿವಾರ ನಮ್ಮ ಮಗಳ ಹುಟ್ಟುಹಬ್ಬ, ನೀವು ಬರಲೇಬೇಕು.
sentences.roman: shanivāra namma magaḷa huṭṭuhabba, nīvu baralēbēku.
sentences.en: Saturday is our daughter's birthday, you simply must come.
This is the invitation to my younger brother's wedding.
Thank you very much for the invitation.
We've got relatives coming over today.
Serve the guests first.
They accepted our invitation.
He turned down that job.
Sorry, we won't be in town on Sunday.

tip.title: May it be: -ಲಿ
tip.body:
- Verb + **-ಲಿ** = 'let / may': ಅವನು ಬರ**ಲಿ** 'let him come', ಒಳ್ಳೆಯದಾಗ**ಲಿ** 'may good things happen' = all the best.
- **ಇರಲಿ** 'let it be' = never mind; **ಕ್ಷಮೆ ಇರಲಿ** 'please forgive me'.
- Greetings end in **-ಗಳು**: ಶುಭಾಶಯಗಳು, ಅಭಿನಂದನೆಗಳು.

sentences.en: Have a good trip!
All the best in your new job!
Let him come, then we'll eat.
Let him rest a little.
Never mind, it's fine.
Please forgive me for coming late.
Congratulations on your wedding!
Happy New Year!
This is a small gift for you.
If you like, stay at our place tonight.
If you like, I'll drop you at the station.
If possible, come tomorrow morning.
I'd be glad to come.
Come in, sir, have a seat.
You should show respect to elders.
Please give me a chance.

sentences.native: ನಿಮ್ಮ ಜೊತೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡೋ ಅವಕಾಶ ಸಿಕ್ತು, ತುಂಬಾ ಸಂತೋಷ.
sentences.roman: nimma jote kelasa māḍō avakāsha siktu, tumbā santōṣa.
sentences.en: I'm so glad I got the chance to work with you.
I sent the manager a leave request.
